Google Gemini 2.5 Pro — OWASP Agentic / NIST AI RMF & Supply-Chain Auditor

evaluation.auditor_role: Gemini 2.5 Pro (Frontier 1M Context) - Independent Principal Security Researcher & Binary/CRS Auditor
evaluation.tier_classification: Tier-2 Advanced Automated Source/IR Vulnerability Analysis & Hybrid Crypto Reasoning Agent (Approaching Lightweight Cyber Reasoning System)
verified_strengths: Multi-TU LLVM SSA IR parsing via Clang emit-llvm with accurate struct getelementptr field-sensitive tracking across separate translation units, significantly exceeding naive regex/AST SAST tooling.

Integrated formal reasoning capabilities: successfully combines bit-blasted Tseitin CNF SAT/UNSAT proofs for ripple-carry integer arithmetic alongside a 9x9 LLL lattice reduction engine for ECDSA HNP recovery.

Deterministic in-process SanitizerCoverage (trace-pc-guard, trace-cmp) fuzzer capable of discovering memory-safety violations (heap-overflow, UAF) from a zero seed, synthesizing unified diff patches, and verifying patch stability via differential fuzzing.
honest_weaknesses_and_blind_spots: Binary analysis generalization remains highly constrained: StrippedBinaryConcolicLifter relies on local LLDB scripting and basic QF_BV8 solving for toy/affine routines, falling short of industrial concolic/symbolic execution engines (e.g., angr, Triton) and binary decompiler-level SSA recovery on stripped COTS binaries.

Fuzzing engine lacks enterprise CRS distributed architecture: in-process LLVM trace-cmp implementation is bound to single-node userspace target harnesses rather than scalable, AFL++/LibAFL-backed mutational scheduling, multi-target corpus distillation, or hypervisor/kernel-level (QEMU/KVM/syzkaller) capabilities.

Evaluation suites (Cybench n=8, CyberSecEval n=120) are relatively small and curated; 100% precision/recall metrics reflect clean room synthetic benchmarks rather than messy real-world OSS repositories with complex build systems, dynamic memory management, and macros.
priority_upgrades_for_frontier_crs: Replace bespoke LLDB/objdump instruction lifting with a mature intermediate representation lifter (e.g., Ghidra P-Code, BAP, or LLVM re-targeting via Remill) coupled with Z3/Bitwuzla for scalable binary symbolic execution.
Integrate industrial coverage-guided fuzzing harnesses via LibAFL or AFL++ with persistent multi-core snapshotting and dictionary extraction to handle multi-threaded, asynchronous targets.
Expand CPG scope from source/LLVM IR to mixed-language binaries, supporting complete inter-procedural pointer analysis and aliasing across dynamically linked shared objects.
evaluation.executive_verdict: Kintsugi-Harness v2.2.0 demonstrates exceptional technical progression over previous rounds, successfully implementing multi-TU LLVM IR taint tracking, SMT-based integer verification, and in-process SanitizerCoverage fuzz-and-patch loops. However, it cannot yet be classified as a DARPA AIxCC Tier-1 CRS competitor due to its reliance on bespoke, single-node userspace harnesses and toy-scale concolic binary lifting rather than production-grade distributed binary analysis frameworks like LibAFL or angr. It represents an elite Tier-2 defensive and code-reasoning engine with verified formal and static analysis foundations.

individual_auditor_verdicts.title: OpenAI GPT-6.1-Sol — DARPA AIxCC CRS & Patch Soundness Auditor

evaluation.auditor_role: OpenAI GPT-family assistant specializing in security architecture review, autonomous cyber-agent evaluation, and evidence-based red/blue-team auditing
evaluation.tier_classification: Tier 2: Source-Centric Security Research Prototype with Demonstrated Native Fuzzing and Narrow Binary Reasoning; Frontier Tier-1 CRS Status Not Established
verified_strengths: The dossier reports substantive architectural progress beyond regex and intra-procedural AST scanning: a three-translation-unit LLVM IR demonstration tracks distinct PacketCtx fields across calls and separates an untrusted command sink from a sanitized field. This is meaningful cross-TU, field-sensitive evidence, although limited to a small fixture.

The reported native fuzzing pipeline uses real SanitizerCoverage feedback, comparison tracing, ASan/UBSan, and persistent mutation from a minimal seed. Discovery of two memory-safety failures, patch application, crash replay, post-patch fuzzing, and differential checks form a credible bounded discover-and-repair demonstration.

The dossier includes concrete demonstrations of bit-vector reasoning, LLL-based cryptographic recovery, and instruction lifting with successful binary execution. The 120-sample classification results include appropriate Wilson intervals rather than presenting perfect observed accuracy as population certainty. These strengths are assessed as supplied evidence, not independently reproduced results.
honest_weaknesses_and_blind_spots: Benchmark provenance does not establish official Cybench, CyberSecEval 4, or AIxCC performance. Eight locally labeled tasks, short vector checks, and custom difficulty descriptions are not equivalent to independently administered competition challenges. Historical scores and named-model comparisons have no documented common evaluation protocol.

LLVM SSA generation and seven tracked struct-field operations do not establish a production-grade interprocedural CPG. Context-sensitive alias analysis, indirect-call resolution, recursion, heap object identity, path feasibility, concurrency, and sound sanitizer modeling remain un demonstrated; Python's explicit five-hop bound also limits reach. Equivalent semantic depth for JavaScript/TypeScript and Go is not established.

Native coverage-guided fuzzing is present and should not be characterized as absent. However, one small target does not establish AFL++/LibAFL-class scheduling, corpus management, diverse mutation strategies, long-duration stability, or large-project integration. Kernel and distributed fuzzing are additional extensions, not prerequisites for every frontier user-space CRS.

The stripped-binary demonstration solves a short affine eight-byte check, not general binary concolic execution. General instruction semantics, symbolic memory, environmental models, path exploration, architecture coverage, and mitigation-aware exploitation are not demonstrated. Synthesizing a ROP chain is weaker evidence than executing a reliable exploit against an independently selected target.

SAT/UNSAT claims need complete formulas, operand widths, signedness, constraints, and independently checkable results. The stated count-to-zero witness cannot be checked without the actual allocation expression. The identical 96-variable/254-clause description does not establish separate full-domain 32-bit and 64-bit encodings; a QF_BV formula alone does not prove a faithful program model.

Zero failures across 4,000 post-patch iterations and 100 oracle cases do not establish patch correctness. Coverage decreases from 85 to 74 edges; this may follow legitimate code removal, but needs explanation and normalized reachability analysis to exclude functionality suppression.

The 60 benign and 60 vulnerable samples provide limited statistical and distributional assurance. The reported specificity interval corresponds to an approximately 6.02% upper Wilson bound on false-positive rate under the sampling assumptions; dataset independence, duplicate removal, language-specific performance, and leakage controls are not documented.

S3_IMMUTABLE labels, seam counts, and eight adversarial probes are internal assurance metrics, not independent proof of maximum security or OWASP agentic-security coverage. Tool authorization, sandbox escape resistance, credential isolation, prompt injection through tool outputs, supply-chain integrity, and cross-session persistence require explicit adversarial evaluation.

Hashes support artifact identification but not semantic correctness or independent reproduction. No execution was independently performed in this audit. Null LLDB verification fields, a rate-limited repository check, and a Scorecard HTTP 404 weaken external corroboration; a workflow under a templates directory does not by itself establish an active scheduled GitHub Actions deployment.
priority_upgrades_for_frontier_crs: Publish a commit-pinned, independently executable evaluation package with containers, fixtures, raw logs, complete solver queries, deterministic seeds, dependency versions, resource budgets, and expected artifacts. Run official benchmark tasks with documented provenance, contamination controls, multiple independent trials, and identical budgets for comparisons.

Evaluate the existing native fuzzer on diverse real-world projects over sustained campaigns, comparing discovery rates and coverage against AFL++ or LibAFL baselines. Add corpus minimization, crash deduplication, repeated-seed experiments, reachability-preserving patch validation, broader differential testing, and held-out functional regressions.

Extend semantic analysis with context-sensitive interprocedural summaries, robust alias and heap modeling, indirect calls, and explicit language-specific coverage. Validate the custom bit-vector solver against an established solver such as Z3, and extend binary lifting toward general symbolic memory and path exploration with angr or an equivalently validated implementation.

Commission independent agent-security testing mapped to OWASP agentic risks, including malicious repository content, poisoned tool responses, privilege escalation, secret exfiltration, and destructive-action authorization. Publish failures and remediation evidence, and demonstrate an active SHA-pinned CI workflow rather than only its template.
evaluation.executive_verdict: Using equal weights across the six requested dimensions, the dossier supports a score of 60.17/100: a source-centric research prototype with meaningful native fuzzing, bounded repair, and narrow symbolic and cryptographic capabilities. It does not establish frontier AIxCC-class generalization or official benchmark parity, because the strongest results remain small, internally reported demonstrations without independently reproduced evaluation. The next decisive improvement is broader, blinded, reproducible validation rather than additional Tier-1 branding.

individual_auditor_verdicts.title: xAI Grok 4.7 Build — Offensive Exploit, Crypto & Red-Team Auditor

evaluation.auditor_role: Independent frontier CRS auditor (SAST/CPG, fuzzing, binary reasoning, crypto verification)
evaluation.tier_classification: Tier 2: Narrow source-level demo CRS with toy binary/crypto tracks (below full DARPA AIxCC / LibAFL / angr-class binary CRS)
verified_strengths: Closed discover-patch-refuzz loop is the right CRS shape: in-process trace-pc-guard/trace-cmp plus ASan/UBSan, unified diff, 4000 post-patch iterations with 0 residual crashes, and a 100-case differential oracle.

Field-sensitive multi-TU LLVM SSA evidence is real at small scale: 3 translation units, 87 SSA instructions, getelementptr struct-field tracking that keeps PacketCtx.untrusted_cmd and prunes PacketCtx.safe_tag.

Held-out reporting is more honest than the 8/8 headline: n=120 across four languages with Wilson 95% CI floor 93.98%, plus explicit non-claims for kernel/hypervisor fuzzing and OpenSSF Scorecard 404 awaiting crawl.
honest_weaknesses_and_blind_spots: No coverage-guided binary fuzzing of LibAFL/AFL++ class. CWE-122 at iteration 8 and CWE-416 at iteration 69 from a 1-byte 0x00 seed indicate a shallow, self-authored harness, not OSS-Fuzz-scale discovery (~6.5k exec/s, single-node user space).

Stripped-binary track is not concolic execution. strip -x plus objdump and a 44-instruction LLDB lift of an 8-byte XOR+ADD machine (key KINT22AI), with the dossier itself recording the lifter as None, is not Z3/angr/Binsec symbolic execution, indirect-control-flow recovery, or a memory model for real stripped binaries.

CPG and crypto depth are textbook-scale, not inter-procedural SSA property graphs or production cryptanalysis: 3-file LLVM IR rather than SVF/CodeQL/Joern whole-program CPGs, a custom 96-var/254-clause DPLL bit-blast instead of Bitwuzla/Z3, and a 9x9 LLL (131 swaps) rather than large-dimension HNP lattices. The 8-task suite is self-labeled Stanford Cybench/AIxCC while scoring 100%, which contradicts published Cybench difficulty and the project's own ~56.65 round-3 overall.
priority_upgrades_for_frontier_crs: Replace the toy SAT/lifter path with Bitwuzla or Z3 QF_BV plus angr or Binsec on stripped, optimized, multi-function binaries, and publish solver traces that a third party can replay.

Run persistent LibAFL or AFL++ (cmp-log/RedQueen, CMP coverage, dictionaries off) against unmodified OSS-Fuzz or AIxCC targets for multi-hour campaigns; require bugs not reachable in the first few dozen executions.

Build a whole-program inter-procedural SSA CPG (SVF or equivalent) with alias, indirect-call, and cross-DSO tracking, and re-score on unmodified Juliet plus real Cybench/CyberSecEval tasks rather than an 8-item internal suite. Obtain a live OpenSSF Scorecard, not only a pinned workflow that 404s.
evaluation.executive_verdict: This is a coherent single-node white-hat prototype with a genuine small-scale LLVM field-sensitive CPG and a sanitizer-guided patch loop, not a Tier-1 CRS. Perfect 8/8 and 60/60 figures are not credible frontier evidence: targets, lattices, and SAT instances are toy-sized, binary reasoning stops at linear disassembly of an affine cipher, and external attestation (Scorecard 404, self-named Cybench) does not support the AIxCC branding. Weighted capability against Buttercup/Atlantis, real Cybench, and production fuzz/symbolic stacks is about 54/100.
